correctness.rationale: The Fourier multiplier \(1_H\) has kernel \(K(x)=\sum_{h\in H}e^{2\pi i hx/p}\). Coset invariance reduces its endpoint norm exactly to the absolute values of the three real cubic Gaussian periods. The inspected period equation gives their three elementary symmetric functions. Depressing the cubic yields the stated trigonometric roots, while the sign of \((p(L+3)-1)/27\), together with the negative second symmetric sum, gives the complete one-positive versus one-negative dichotomy. Substitution proves both branches. The standalone computation replays the identities for all eighty eligible primes below \(1001\), but the finite check is only corroborative.

value.rationale: The frequency set is the canonical index-three multiplicative subgroup, not an arbitrary finite slice. Its projection is the first nonquadratic cyclotomic analogue in which the nonzero kernel values are three distinct Gaussian periods. The exact endpoint stability constant is therefore a natural harmonic invariant. The result exposes a qualitative feature absent from the quadratic-residue case: the norm changes arithmetic branch according to the sign pattern of the periods, governed by the integer \(L\) in \(4p=L^2+27M^2\). This is a structural all-prime formula rather than a table recomputation.
